stories.title: Paladin Expands SoCal Workforce Portfolio with Bellflower Acquisition
stories.excerpt: Paladin Realty Partners LLC, has expanded its growing workforce rental housing portfolio in Southern California with the recent acquisition of Brownstone Apartments, a 17-unit apartment community located in Bellflower. Built in 1967, the property has nine one-bedroom units, seven two-bedroom units and a studio unit. As with its previous SoCal workforce housing investments, Paladin intends to pursue a value-added business plan to modernize the property. “While on the smaller side for us, Brownstone Apartments is exactly the type of opportunity we seek in Southern California,” said Fred Gortner, Co-Founder and Head of U.S. Strategy at Paladin Realty. “It’s a well-located, well-maintained but under-managed asset in a prime workforce housing submarket. Our objective is to upgrade the asset and enhance the residents’ quality of life, while preserving critically needed affordable workforce housing in a highly desirable infill location.” California Bank & Trust provided the debt financing. Bridgeport Investments in Newport Beach served as a financial advisor to Paladin. Tracy Hong and Chris Keramati at Trigor Group brokered the transaction. The post Paladin Expands SoCal Workforce Portfolio with Bellflower Acquisition appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Paladin Realty acquires 17-unit Brownstone Apartments in Bellflower, CA workforce housing.
Value-add strategy targets under-managed but well-located SoCal workforce rental assets.
California Bank & Trust provides debt financing; Trigor Group brokered transaction.
stories.summary: Paladin Realty Partners acquired Brownstone Apartments, a 17-unit 1967-built property in Bellflower, CA, as part of its expanding workforce housing portfolio in Southern California. The property comprises nine one-bedroom, seven two-bedroom, and one studio unit. Paladin plans a value-add modernization while preserving affordability.
stories.impact: Signals continued investor appetite for small, under-managed workforce housing assets in SoCal submarkets where supply is constrained and affordability pressure is acute. This tuck-in acquisition strategy (typical for institutional buyers) suggests Paladin sees market inefficiency in scattered, aging units—opportunity for development teams to identify similar pocket listings before larger players consolidate them.

stories.title: Walker & Dunlop Arranges Refi on Newly Built Bed-Stuy Multifamily
stories.excerpt: Walker & Dunlop, Inc. arranged a $137.5-million refinancing for 12 Halsey, a newly completed Class A mixed-use multifamily property located in Brooklyn’s Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood. Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory advised EJS Group and Hope Street Capital in arranging the three-year, floating-rate financing with AllianceBernstein. Aaron Appel, Jonathan Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Dustin Stolly, Sean Reimer, Michael Diaz, Michael Ianno, and Cole Grims led the refinancing. “Demand for newly constructed multifamily assets in New York City remains exceptionally strong, particularly for properties that combine high-quality execution, affordability, and transit-oriented locations,” said Appel. “12 Halsey represents exactly the type of institutional-quality asset that continues to attract significant lender interest.” Completed in October 2025, 12 Halsey comprises 240 residential units, with 30% designated as affordable, along with approximately 2,400 square feet of ground-floor retail. The property occupies a full cross-block site between Fulton and Halsey streets and benefits from immediate access to the A and C subway lines. The post Walker & Dunlop Arranges Refi on Newly Built Bed-Stuy Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Walker & Dunlop arranges $137.5M refi on 12 Halsey, 240-unit newly completed mixed-use in Bed-Stuy, Brooklyn.
30% of units designated affordable; three-year floating-rate financing from AllianceBernstein.
Property completed October 2025; transit-oriented, A/C subway access, ground-floor retail.
stories.summary: Walker & Dunlop arranged a $137.5 million three-year floating-rate refinancing for 12 Halsey, a newly completed 240-unit Class A mixed-use property in Brooklyn's Bed-Stuy neighborhood. The property includes 30% affordable units, 2,400 SF ground-floor retail, and sits at a full cross-block site between Fulton and Halsey with immediate subway access. Financing was secured from AllianceBernstein.
stories.impact: Strong lender appetite for newly built, mixed-income, transit-rich multifamily in NYC's outer-borough markets signals durable demand and healthy underwriting fundamentals even at floating rates. Bed-Stuy's trajectory (cultural amenities, young demographic, transit nodes) supports pricing power and absorption; development teams should accelerate similar transit-oriented affordability plays in Queens and Bronx before land costs escalate further.

stories.title: IPA Team Closes Sale of Pomona Multifamily
stories.excerpt: Institutional Property Advisors (IPA), a division of Marcus & Millichap dedicated to serving the company’s institutional clients, closed the sale of Terramonte at Foothill, a 138-unit multifamily asset in Pomona. The $36.7-million sale price represents $265,942 per unit. “The sale is one of only four 100-plus-unit, market-rate multifamily transactions to have occurred in Pomona over the past five years,” said Kevin Green IPA executive director. Green, Zorbas, Joseph Grabiec, Alexander Garcia Jr., and Greg Harris of IPA represented the seller, Positive Investments, and procured the buyer, Sack Capital Partners. The property is located on Foothill Boulevard/State Route 66 off State Route 210, near Interstate 10. These freeways, and the nearby Montclair TransCenter, Pomona Transit Center, and Pomona-North Metrolink station give residents transportation options to employment centers in Los Angeles and throughout the Inland Empire. California State Polytechnic University, Pomona, the University of La Verne, Western University of Health Sciences, and the Claremont Colleges surround the property. The post IPA Team Closes Sale of Pomona Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: IPA closes sale of Terramonte at Foothill, 138-unit Pomona multifamily for $36.7M ($265,942/unit).
One of only four 100+ unit market-rate sales in Pomona in past five years.
Transit access via Metrolink, TransCenter, and proximity to Cal Poly Pomona, regional universities.
stories.summary: Institutional Property Advisors closed the sale of Terramonte at Foothill, a 138-unit market-rate multifamily asset in Pomona, CA, to Sack Capital Partners for $36.7 million ($265,942 per unit). The property is one of only four 100+ unit market-rate multifamily transactions in Pomona over the past five years. It benefits from freeway access (I-10, Route 210), Metrolink station proximity, and nearby university anchors.
stories.impact: Pomona's thin transaction volume for large multifamily (4 deals/5 years) combined with university and employment-center proximity signals undersupply and limited new development pipeline. Inland Empire developers should view Pomona as a blue-chip submarket for new construction—transit, anchors, and scarcity support rent growth and feasibility even at current cost structures.

stories.title: BFC, SAA Canopy Land $269M Financing for Syracuse Redevelopment
stories.excerpt: BFC Partners and SAA Canopy Group have closed on a $269-million construction loan to transform the long-standing Parkside Commons housing complex on Syracuse’s East Side. The project will deliver a total of 393 affordable apartments through a combination of renovated and newly constructed housing. “Our mission at BFC is to create high-quality affordable housing that enhances the quality of life for the families who call our communities home,” said Winthrop Wharton, principal, BFC Partners. “Parkside Commons is poised for a transformative new chapter, and we are proud to partner with New York State to deliver the substantial investments this community deserves.” The property currently consists of 10 buildings spanning Westmoreland and East Fayette Streets, and the loan will enable BFC Partners and SAA Canopy to simultaneously renovate six of those buildings and construct two new ones. The new buildings will provide enough space to relocate every current resident of the four oldest structures on the site, which will then be demolished. Once that land is cleared, it will become the site of additional housing in a later development phase. The post BFC, SAA Canopy Land $269M Financing for Syracuse Redevelopment appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: BFC Partners and SAA Canopy close $269M construction loan for Parkside Commons transformation, Syracuse.
393 affordable units: renovate 6 buildings, construct 2 new; demolish 4 oldest structures.
New York State partnership; phased development with future additional housing on cleared land.
stories.summary: BFC Partners and SAA Canopy closed a $269 million construction loan to transform Parkside Commons, a long-standing affordable housing complex on Syracuse's East Side. The project will deliver 393 affordable apartments through simultaneous renovation of six buildings and construction of two new ones; four oldest structures will be demolished to clear land for future phases. The deal reflects substantial New York State investment in legacy property repositioning.
stories.impact: Major state-backed capital flows into rust-belt legacy affordable housing signal public sector confidence in demand stabilization and opportunity for private developers to partner on similar urban infill plays. Pomona's high institutional interest, combined with Syracuse's public backing, suggests secondary metros with university/civic anchors and aging stock are becoming development targets—but regulatory and entitlement timelines remain extended.

stories.title: Rockland Trust Lends on Acquisition of Kingston Country Club
stories.excerpt: Rockland Trust financed the acquisition of Indian Pond Country Club (IPCC), a private championship golf club in Kingston, MA. The buyer, Bobby Palma, is a Kingston native, longtime IPCC member and South Shore entrepreneur with deep ties to the region. The Boston Business Journal reported the sale price as $12 million. “IPCC has been a special place for me for many years, not only as a member, but as someone who grew up here in Kingston and cares deeply about this community. Owning the club is both a personal honor and a significant responsibility,” said Palma.“I’m grateful to Rockland Trust for their partnership and support in helping make this vision a reality.” Founded in 2001, IPCC is set among wooded conservation land and the Indian Pond Estates residential community. Indian Pond’s experienced management team will continue to oversee daily operations across golf, dining, events, and facilities. The post Rockland Trust Lends on Acquisition of Kingston Country Club appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Rockland Trust finances acquisition of Indian Pond Country Club, Kingston, MA for $12M.
Buyer: Bobby Palma, local entrepreneur; club founded 2001, set in conservation land.
No multifamily development or redevelopment disclosed; golf/hospitality asset only.
stories.summary: Rockland Trust financed Bobby Palma's $12 million acquisition of Indian Pond Country Club (IPCC), a private championship golf club in Kingston, MA, founded in 2001. Palma, a local entrepreneur and IPCC member, plans to operate the property with its existing management team overseeing golf, dining, events, and facilities.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. Golf club ownership and hospitality operations fall outside core residential real estate strategy; no conversion, redevelopment, or housing implications announced. Monitor only if site future zoning or land use changes emerge.

stories.title: TekSynap Leases 27K SF at BXP’s Reston Town Center
stories.excerpt: Federal IT contractor TekSynap has signed a long-term lease for a 26,500-square-foot floor at BXP’s Reston Town Center in Northern Virginia. TekSynap provides cloud integration, cybersecurity, software development and IT modernization services for civilian, defense and intelligence agencies. The Reston-based company will relocate less than a mile from 1900 Oracle Way to the second floor of 11921 Freedom Drive. The new office will house TekSynap’s core services team and serve as what the company described as a digital nerve center for its operations. TekSynap employs about 1,800 people, including subcontractors. The transaction marks another office lease at BXP’s 5 million-square-foot Reston Town Center mixed-use campus. “TekSynap’s move to Reston Town Center underscores the demand for workplaces that combine high-quality office space with a vibrant, amenity-rich environment,” Erin Cotter, BXP’s vice president of office leasing, said in a statement. TekSynap CEO Kam Jinnah said the relocation reflects the company’s rapid expansion in the government technology sector, particularly as artificial intelligence reshapes information technology. “Our growth has not come easily; it has been earned through technical excellence, responsiveness, and an unwavering commitment to our customers’ missions,” Jinnah said in a statement. “Taking major space in the heart of the Reston Town Center is a meaningful milestone for our company.” Cole Spalding of Newmark represented TekSynap in the lease and announced the deal on Monday. Reston Town Center includes approximately 50 retailers, more than 30 restaurants and a newer expansion adjacent to the Silver Line’s Metro station with two office towers, the 39-story Skymark apartment tower, dual-branded Marriott hotels and 60,000 square feet of retail. bullets: Federal IT contractor TekSynap leases 26,500 SF floor at BXP's Reston Town Center, Northern Virginia.
Relocation within Reston (less than 1 mile); TekSynap employs ~1,800 people including subcontractors.
Office lease underscores demand for amenity-rich mixed-use campuses; no residential component noted.
stories.summary: Federal IT contractor TekSynap signed a long-term lease for 26,500 square feet at BXP's Reston Town Center, relocating less than a mile from its prior Oracle Way location. The company employs approximately 1,800 people and provides cloud integration, cybersecurity, and IT modernization services for defense and civilian agencies. The lease marks continued office demand at the 5 million-square-foot mixed-use campus.
stories.impact: Office leasing at Reston Town Center is not a direct demand signal for multifamily development, but employer stability and expansion in fed-contractor hubs (Northern Virginia) support long-term population retention and rental demand in submarkets with limited new supply. Existing mixed-use assets (like Reston) will absorb office tenants; development teams should focus on residential in transit-connected secondary Reston/Tysons locations where office-residential separation is widening.

stories.title: University of California Buys 16 Westwood Village Properties for $50M
stories.excerpt: The University of California is extending its streak of commercial real estate investment after acquiring a 16-property portfolio immediately south of UCLA in Los Angeles. The Regents of the University of California, which governs the state’s university system, put down $49.8 million for the properties in Westwood Village, Atlas Brief reported. The portfolio includes 181,855 square feet of retail, office and open space on about 2.6 acres mostly along Westwood Boulevard, as well as on Kinross Avenue, Gayley Avenue and Lindbrook Drive. One property at 1000-1010 Westwood Boulevard spans 64,491 square feet and traded for about $5.75 million, or $89 per square foot. Another property, the historic Kinross Cornerstone, was built in 1930, but has been renovated. No specific plan for the properties has been publicly announced. Representatives for UC Regents did not immediately return a request for comment. Anderson Real Estate, the family-owned real estate company tied to the late John E. Anderson, sold the portfolio. The Anderson family gave more than $140 million to UCLA, built the business organization that included Topa Equities, and co-founded investment firm Kayne Anderson. UCLA’s business school is named after Anderson. The portfolio gives the Regents more commercial assets on the Westside, one of L.A.’s most difficult markets for assembling land. UCLA is transforming the former Westside Pavilion into a 700,000-square-foot research park after acquiring the property for $700 million two and a half years ago. UCLA also acquired Downtown L.A.’s historic 334,000-square-foot Trust Building three years ago to expand classrooms and administrative offices. And, in November 2024, UCLA paid $55 million for a 170,000-square-foot South Bay office property for a $90 million redevelopment into the UCLA Health Sports Medicine Institute. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: University of California acquires 16-property portfolio in Westwood Village for $49.8M (181,855 SF).
Properties on Westwood Blvd, Kinross, Gayley, Lindbrook; include historic 1930 Kinross Cornerstone.
No public development plan disclosed; institutional anchor play adjacent to UCLA campus.
stories.summary: The University of California Regents purchased a 16-property portfolio in Westwood Village, Los Angeles, for $49.8 million comprising 181,855 square feet of retail, office, and open space across approximately 2.6 acres. Properties are located primarily along Westwood Boulevard and nearby streets immediately south of the UCLA campus. One flagship property at 1000-1010 Westwood Boulevard traded at $89 per square foot; the historic Kinross Cornerstone (1930) was included.
stories.impact: UC's strategic land assembly in Westwood Village signals intent to control mixed-use development opportunities adjacent to a major anchor tenant and enrollment base. This institutional landbanking limits near-term multifamily supply in the submarket and could presage future UC-sponsored mixed-income housing. Development teams should monitor UC's master plan; opportunities to partner on student/faculty housing remain but competitive landscape will tighten as UC consolidates control.

stories.title: Mixed-Use Upper West Side Building Sells to Terra Developers for $28M
stories.excerpt: Brooklyn-based Terra Developers has made a $28 million residential redevelopment play for 500 Columbus Avenue on Manhattan’s Upper West Side. The 35,300-square-foot mixed-use building was sold to Terra by longtime owner CKMR Corporation, formerly Sloan’s Supermarkets, according to property records filed Friday. The property rises five stories at the northwest corner of West 84th Street and Columbus Avenue, just one block west of Central Park. Its ground-floor retail is anchored by a Gristedes supermarket, above which sits a dozen apartment units that have been vacant for 30 years, BKREA’s Bob Knakal told Commercial Observer. Knakal, the founder of BKREA and the exclusive listing agent for the property, said 500 Columbus Avenue’s residential spaces are well positioned for conversion into condominiums. An additional vertical expansion upon the 10,217-square-foot corner lot is possible, according to the BKREA listing. Yevgeniy Lvovskiy, CEO of ZHL Group, confirmed the purchase on behalf of Terra, but did not disclose Terra’s plans for the site. ZHL previously represented Terra and other investment partners in the $27.6 million purchase of a Long Island City, Queens, redevelopment site in 2024. The building at 500 Columbus Avenue was last sold in the 1970s to an entity of Sloan’s Supermarkets, founded by the Sloan and Meyer families. CKMR now manages legacy assets across New York City. Lucia Nuzzi-Meyer served as CKMR’s authorized signatory in the recent transaction. Representatives for CKMR could not immediately be reached for comment. Additional retail tenants at 500 Columbus Avenue include Park West Laundromat and a shoe repair shop. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Terra Developers acquires mixed-use 500 Columbus Avenue, Upper West Side Manhattan for $28M.
35,300 SF, 5-story building; 12 residential units vacant 30 years; Gristedes-anchored retail.
Bob Knakal identified conversion-to-condo opportunity; vertical expansion possible on corner lot.
stories.summary: Brooklyn-based Terra Developers purchased 500 Columbus Avenue on Manhattan's Upper West Side for $28 million, a 35,300-square-foot mixed-use building at the northwest corner of West 84th Street and Columbus Avenue. The property features Gristedes supermarket ground-floor retail and 12 residential units that have been vacant for 30 years. Listing agent Bob Knakal noted the residential spaces are well-positioned for condo conversion; vertical expansion is also possible.
stories.impact: Upper West Side's supply constraints and condo conversion dynamics favor small, well-located mixed-use infill plays like this. However, Terra's acquisition signals developer focus on condo conversion and value-add rather than multifamily rental development—limited direct demand signal for apartment supply growth. Watch for any master-plan residential rental components; if Terra pursues rental, it signals confidence in UWS rental fundamentals despite condo trend.

stories.title: CIP Real Estate Buys Broward Campus for $99M
stories.excerpt: CIP Real Estate has paid $99 million for an industrial and office park in Broward County, Fla., property records show. Called Lyons Business Park, the property includes about 10 buildings, totaling 338,000 square feet It’s located at 6601 Lyons Road in Coconut Creek, Fla., near the corner with Johnson Road, about a mile west of Florida’s Turnpike. BMO Bank, serving as an administrative agent for a group of lenders, supplied a $66.9 million acquisition loan, which is scheduled to mature in 2029. A vacant, 3,000-square-foot warehouse is currently on the market for $23 a square foot. The sellers, an entity tied to Tiffany and Lee Lasser and others, appear to have owned the 26-acre campus since the 1990s and early 2000s. The acquisition marks the second South Florida purchase for Irvine, Calif.-based CIP Real Estate in the past year, after it paid $47 million to acquire two small-bay warehouses in Hialeah from TA Realty. In 2024, the firm raised $300 million to expand its industrial footprint into the Southeast. Representatives for CIP Real Estate did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while the sellers could not be reached for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: CIP Real Estate buys Lyons Business Park, Coconut Creek, FL for $99M (338,000 SF, ~10 buildings).
BMO Bank provides $66.9M acquisition loan (maturity 2029); 26-acre industrial/office campus.
Second South Florida purchase for CIP in one year; firm raised $300M in 2024 for Southeast expansion.
stories.summary: CIP Real Estate acquired Lyons Business Park in Coconut Creek, FL, for $99 million, an industrial and office park comprising approximately 10 buildings and 338,000 square feet on a 26-acre campus. BMO Bank supplied a $66.9 million acquisition loan maturing in 2029. This marks CIP's second South Florida purchase in one year and reflects the firm's broader $300 million Southeast industrial expansion capital raise in 2024.
stories.impact: CIP's repeated South Florida industrial acquisitions signal strong capital deployment in Broward logistics and light-industrial markets ahead of broader Southeast supply tightness. Development teams should note: institutional investors are consolidating established parks; new build opportunities increasingly favor infill urban locations or emerging I-4 corridor sites where land costs remain favorable. Expect competitive bidding pressure on aging, well-located industrial assets in legacy markets.

stories.title: LMXD, BedRock Secure $250M Loan for 560-Unit Astoria Housing Project
stories.excerpt: LMXD and BedRock Real Estate Partners have closed on a $250 million loan to facilitate the purchase and construction of a housing development in Astoria, Queens, Commercial Observer has learned. The financing from New York Life Investment Management gets the wheels turning on the development of 560 mixed-income housing units at 35-10 Steinway Street, as well as a new retail location for a P.C. Richard & Son store in the neighborhood, according to the developers. “We are excited to move forward with our plan to bring mixed-income housing, including permanently affordable homes, to Steinway Street and contribute to the responsible growth of this vibrant neighborhood,” a spokesperson for LMXD and BedRock said in a statement. BedRock and LMXD acquired the site, which includes 35-18 Steinway Street, for $53 million last week. JLL‘s Rob Hinckley, Scott Aiese, Jeffrey Julien, Lauren Kaufman and Alex Staikos arranged the new financing for the transaction. “High-quality developments with strong sponsorship and solid fundamentals continue to attract institutional capital, and Steinway Crossing is a prime example,” Hinckley said in a statement. New York Life did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Apartment units in the Astoria project will range from studios to three-bedrooms, and 25 percent will be set aside as affordable housing for those earning an average of 60 percent of the area median income. The building will be designed by Beyer Blinder Belle Architects & Planners with all-electric infrastructure. However, the more interesting aspect of the development is that it falls within the section of land rezoned through a 2022 Uniform Land Use Review Procedure as part of the defunct Innovation QNS project by Silverstein Properties. bullets: LMXD and BedRock close $250M construction loan (New York Life) for 560-unit Astoria project, Queens.
35-10 Steinway Street; mixed-income units with permanent affordability; P.C. Richard retail component.
Developers acquired site for $53M prior week; loan enables purchase and full development.
stories.summary: LMXD and BedRock Real Estate Partners closed a $250 million construction loan from New York Life Investment Management to finance the purchase and development of a 560-unit mixed-income housing project at 35-10 Steinway Street in Astoria, Queens. The project will include permanently affordable units and a new P.C. Richard & Son retail location. Developers had acquired the site (35-18 Steinway Street included) for $53 million the prior week.
stories.impact: Strong institutional capital availability for mixed-income Queens development signals sustained confidence in outer-borough rental fundamentals and affordability mandates. Astoria's transit proximity, young demographic, and limited new supply support absorption; however, the project's large scale and blended affordability model suggest compressed returns—development teams should target smaller, faster-moving sites or focus on submarkets (Sunset Park, Astoria North) where affordability requirements are less dense and value-add plays remain viable.
